subject: Variance-driven GPU sizing & deal augmentation
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@stellaris.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing check-in: Q2 utilization spike and renewal window

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. I pulled together our Q2 utilization and there are a few surprises: sustained peak traffic for a 48hr window mid-June that pushed our 95th p99 latency up and consumed ~22% more GPU-hours than forecasted. I attached the CSV export.

We're approaching our renewal window (end of August) and Procurement wants to understand options: do we add reserved GPUs now, convert part of our burst to committed, or add short-term burst buffers for seasonality? Our finance lead is sensitive to multi-month commits but we also need to avoid disruption during peak ML experiments.

Would appreciate a short runbook / recommendations and a ballpark delta on committed GPUs required to keep 99th below target for expected growth (we expect similar experiment cadence in Q3).

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Park
Director of ML Ops, Stellaris AI

Attachment: stellaris_Q2_utilization_report.csv
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@stellaris.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing check-in: Q2 utilization spike and renewal window

Lena —

Thanks for the data, this is helpful. I reviewed the CSV and summarized key points below; attaching a short proposal (proposed_capacity_amendment_v1.pdf) that outlines three options. Quick summary:

- Immediate buffer: +8 committed GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equiv) to eliminate the 48hr tail risk and give headroom for similar bursts.
- Seasonal burst pool: keep current commit, add a 4–6 GPU burst buffer for 2 months during expected experimentation windows (lower CAPEX commitment).
- Hybrid: +4 committed GPUs + 4 GPU burst pool (recommended if finance tolerates a small commit).

Ballpark economics in the attachment show hybrid reduces expected overage charges by ~45% vs no-change while increasing committed costs by ~18% monthly.

Ben / Karthik — can you validate the risk assumptions and check whether the hybrid would be feasible from a provisioning perspective? I tried to map to Stellaris's existing tranche.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_capacity_amendment_v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@stellaris.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing check-in: Q2 utilization spike and renewal window

Lena / team —

I ran a quick utilization translate based on the CSV and Soojin's proposal. Key numbers:

- Current committed GPUs: 40
- Observed peak 48hr equivalent: ~49 GPU-hours effective -> suggests shortfall of ~6–9 GPUs for sustained window (matching Soojin's +8 immediate buffer).
- If Stellaris expects 15% month-over-month growth in model runs, recommended commit growth over the renewal year is 6 GPUs now + review in Q4.

If we go hybrid (+4 commit, +4 burst), we can front-load a smaller commit to stay within Procurement's budget constraints while allowing burst coverage for experiments. I'll prepare a short amendment draft for Procurement that frames the hybrid as a 6-month pilot with renewal fallback clauses.

Marissa — need legal/sales approval on the pilot clause language and discounting bands. Lena — I can get a binding amendment template and estimated monthly delta by EOD tomorrow if that helps your procurement timeline.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Lena Park <lena.park@stellaris.ai>
Date: 2026-07-11T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing check-in: Q2 utilization spike and renewal window

Quick tech note from capacity/op side:

- The hybrid is operationally clean — we can reserve +4 GPUs to the customer's dedicated pool immediately and reserve a 4-GPU burst pool in the same region. The burst pool will be routed by priority-based scheduling so sustained jobs that exceed commit will be throttled to preserve latency SLOs for high-priority traffic.
- Observed risk: if experiments continue to run long stateful jobs, burst will fill quickly; recommend an autoscale policy with a max-job-duration guard and a KV cache warm-start suggestion to reduce repetition.

I'll update the capacity playbook with these operational constraints and hand over a routing policy snippet for your ops team. From provisioning lead time, we can spin up the extra reserved GPUs within 7 business days once the PO/amendment is approved.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@stellaris.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Variance-driven GPU sizing & deal augmentation

Lena —

Thanks for surfacing this and thanks team for the quick analysis. From a commercial perspective, proposing the hybrid 6-month pilot gives Stellaris the flexibility to validate the delta without a long-term commit. Suggested next steps:

1) Ben to send a one-page amendment (pilot terms + rollback guardrails) and a PO-friendly cost table by EOD 7/13.
2) Karthik to provide the routing policy snippet and a provisioning ETA (7 business days) for the +4 reserved GPUs.
3) Soojin to shepherd a short kickoff call with Stellaris Ops to align on job-duration caps and burst rules.

If Procurement approves the pilot PO, we can target provisioning the reserve in the week of 7/20 and enable the burst pool immediately.

Marissa Cole
Director, Renewals & Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
